name: Giotto
bio: Italian painter whose frescoes helped introduce convincing human feeling into medieval art.
style: Solid figures, clear spatial staging, and direct emotional gestures.

name: Duccio
bio: Sienese painter who combined Byzantine traditions with emerging Italian naturalism.
style: Gold grounds, flowing contours, delicate color, and devotional intimacy.

name: Fra Angelico
bio: Early Renaissance Florentine friar and painter of devotional scenes.
style: Luminous color, restrained perspective, and contemplative sacred spaces.

name: Masaccio
bio: Florentine painter whose work advanced Renaissance perspective and modeling.
style: Architectural perspective, weighty figures, and unified light.

name: Sandro Botticelli
bio: Florentine Renaissance painter of religious and mythological subjects.
style: Elegant contour, rhythmic figures, and poetic mythological settings.

name: Leonardo da Vinci
bio: Italian Renaissance painter and investigator of nature and human anatomy.
style: Sfumato, subtle expression, atmospheric depth, and closely observed forms.

name: Michelangelo
bio: Italian Renaissance painter, sculptor, and architect.
style: Monumental anatomy, sculptural bodies, and dramatic gesture.

name: Raphael
bio: Italian High Renaissance painter known for harmonious figures and compositions.
style: Balanced perspective, graceful figures, and lucid spatial harmony.

name: Titian
bio: Venetian Renaissance painter celebrated for color and expressive brushwork.
style: Rich layered color, dynamic figures, and sensuous light.

name: Tintoretto
bio: Venetian painter whose dramatic compositions bridge Renaissance and Mannerist art.
style: Steep diagonals, theatrical illumination, and energetic groups.

name: El Greco
bio: Cretan-born painter who developed a distinctive style in Spain.
work: The Burial of the Count of Orgaz
style: Elongated figures, visionary space, and intense spiritual color.

name: Caravaggio
bio: Italian Baroque painter who brought ordinary human presence into sacred scenes.
style: Sharp chiaroscuro, theatrical light, and unsentimental naturalism.

name: Artemisia Gentileschi
bio: Italian Baroque painter known for forceful biblical heroines.
style: Dramatic chiaroscuro, physical action, and psychologically focused women.

name: Sofonisba Anguissola
bio: Italian Renaissance painter celebrated for portraits and family scenes.
style: Attentive portraiture, informal gesture, and subtle interpersonal drama.

name: Pieter Bruegel the Elder
bio: Netherlandish painter of peasant life, landscapes, and moral allegories.
style: Panoramic landscapes, busy human detail, and seasonal atmosphere.

name: Hieronymus Bosch
bio: Netherlandish painter known for fantastical religious and moral imagery.
style: Fantastic creatures, densely populated worlds, and unsettling allegory.

name: Jan van Eyck
bio: Early Netherlandish painter whose oil technique enabled exceptional detail.
style: Luminous oil glazes, minute surfaces, and symbolic domestic objects.

name: Albrecht Dürer
bio: German Renaissance painter and printmaker who studied proportion and nature.
style: Precise contours, meticulous textures, and measured Renaissance geometry.

name: Hans Holbein the Younger
bio: German-born Renaissance painter known for portraits at the English court.
style: Exact likeness, finely described objects, and intellectual symbolism.

name: Diego Velázquez
bio: Spanish Baroque court painter whose portraits probe seeing and representation.
style: Economical brushwork, complex viewpoints, and luminous spatial realism.

name: Rembrandt
bio: Dutch painter and printmaker whose work explores human vulnerability.
style: Warm chiaroscuro, layered paint, and psychologically searching faces.

name: Johannes Vermeer
bio: Dutch painter of quiet domestic interiors.
style: Pearlescent light, still compositions, and finely balanced color.

name: Peter Paul Rubens
bio: Flemish Baroque painter of dynamic religious and mythological scenes.
style: Muscular motion, sweeping diagonals, and warm abundant color.

name: Frans Hals
bio: Dutch Golden Age painter known for lively portraiture.
style: Quick visible strokes, animated expressions, and informal presence.

name: Judith Leyster
bio: Dutch Golden Age painter of portraits and everyday entertainments.
style: Lively gesture, warm light, and confident loose brushwork.

name: Nicolas Poussin
bio: French painter active in Rome who pursued classical order.
style: Measured composition, classical figures, and restrained emotional narrative.

name: Antoine Watteau
bio: French painter whose fêtes galantes depict theatrical sociability.
style: Feathery brushwork, theatrical elegance, and wistful pastoral gatherings.

name: Jean-Baptiste-Siméon Chardin
bio: French painter known for still lifes and quiet domestic scenes.
style: Humble objects, muted harmonies, and patient attention to texture.

name: Élisabeth Vigée Le Brun
bio: French portrait painter who worked across European courts.
style: Graceful poses, soft light, and cultivated portrait intimacy.

name: Francisco Goya
bio: Spanish painter and printmaker whose work spans court portraiture and social nightmare.
style: Expressive darkness, unidealized humanity, and unsettling political witness.

name: J. M. W. Turner
bio: British Romantic painter who explored light, weather, and modern change.
style: Dissolving forms, luminous atmosphere, and turbulent natural forces.

name: John Constable
bio: English Romantic painter associated with landscapes of rural Suffolk.
style: Observed skies, broken green tones, and intimate rural landscapes.

name: Eugène Delacroix
bio: French Romantic painter whose works emphasize color and dramatic movement.
style: Energetic color, sweeping motion, and charged historical scenes.

name: Gustave Courbet
bio: French Realist painter who made ordinary people subjects of monumental painting.
style: Earthy color, physical materiality, and unidealized everyday subjects.

name: Jean-François Millet
bio: French painter associated with the Barbizon school and rural labor.
style: Solid peasant figures, quiet earth tones, and dignified daily work.

name: Kamal-ol-Molk
bio: Iranian painter associated with naturalistic painting in the Qajar period.
style: Detailed interiors, careful perspective, and finely observed reflected light.

name: Édouard Manet
bio: French painter whose modern subjects helped open the way to Impressionism.
style: Flat tonal contrasts, modern urban subjects, and ambiguous viewpoints.

name: Claude Monet
bio: French Impressionist painter who repeatedly studied light over familiar landscapes.
style: Broken color, atmospheric light, and repeated observations of nature.

name: Pierre-Auguste Renoir
bio: French Impressionist painter known for social scenes and sensuous color.
work: Bal du moulin de la Galette
style: Warm color, flickering sunlight, and convivial human groups.

name: Edgar Degas
bio: French painter whose work studies dancers, urban life, and unconventional viewpoints.
style: Cropped framing, asymmetrical composition, and closely studied movement.

name: Berthe Morisot
bio: French Impressionist painter of domestic life, leisure, and landscape.
style: Airy brushwork, luminous whites, and intimate everyday scenes.

name: Mary Cassatt
bio: American Impressionist painter active in France, known for women and children.
style: Intimate figures, patterned surfaces, and perspectives influenced by Japanese prints.

name: Alfred Sisley
bio: British Impressionist painter who spent most of his career in France.
style: Quiet river landscapes, luminous skies, and delicate shifting color.

name: Camille Pissarro
bio: Caribbean-born French Impressionist painter of rural and urban life.
style: Broken brushwork, everyday labor, and expansive city views.

name: Paul Cézanne
bio: French painter whose structured observations helped shape modern art.
style: Geometric structure, shifting viewpoints, and constructive color planes.

name: Vincent van Gogh
bio: Dutch Post-Impressionist painter who transformed observation through color and gesture.
style: Impasto, animated contours, and emotionally charged complementary colors.

name: Paul Gauguin
bio: French Post-Impressionist painter who worked in Brittany and the Pacific.
work: Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?
style: Flat color, simplified forms, and symbolic arrangements.

name: Georges Seurat
bio: French painter who developed a systematic division of color.
work: A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte
style: Pointillist marks, optical color, and carefully ordered figures.

name: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec
bio: French painter and printmaker who portrayed Parisian nightlife.
style: Graphic contours, cropped compositions, and candid urban figures.

name: Odilon Redon
bio: French Symbolist artist whose images move between dream and nature.
style: Dreamlike creatures, floating forms, and glowing symbolic color.

name: Edvard Munch
bio: Norwegian painter whose work explores anxiety, intimacy, and mortality.
style: Sinuous contours, stark color, and psychologically charged landscapes.

name: Gustav Klimt
bio: Austrian painter associated with the Vienna Secession.
style: Gold ornament, patterned surfaces, and flattened intimate figures.

name: Egon Schiele
bio: Austrian Expressionist painter known for intense portraits and figure studies.
style: Angular bodies, exposed line, and uneasy psychological intimacy.

name: Henri Matisse
bio: French painter whose work made color an independent expressive force.
style: Bold flat color, simplified forms, and rhythmic spatial balance.

name: Pablo Picasso
bio: Spanish painter who helped develop Cubism and worked across many modern styles.
style: Fractured viewpoints, reinvented figures, and forceful visual symbolism.

name: Georges Braque
bio: French painter who developed Cubism with Picasso.
style: Fragmented objects, shallow space, and muted geometric planes.

name: Wassily Kandinsky
bio: Russian-born painter who helped establish abstract art.
style: Musical color relationships, dynamic shapes, and nonrepresentational movement.

name: Kazimir Malevich
bio: Russian avant-garde painter and founder of Suprematism.
style: Geometric abstraction, stark fields, and radical reduction of form.

name: Piet Mondrian
bio: Dutch painter associated with De Stijl and geometric abstraction.
style: Primary colors, rectilinear grids, and rhythmic visual balance.

name: Paul Klee
bio: Swiss-born painter whose inventive visual language joins abstraction and figuration.
style: Playful signs, delicate lines, and poetic color structures.

name: Marc Chagall
bio: Belarusian-born French painter whose images draw on Jewish life and memory.
style: Floating figures, dreamlike scale, and luminous narrative color.

name: Salvador Dalí
bio: Spanish Surrealist painter known for sharply rendered dream imagery.
style: Precise illusionism, improbable objects, and elastic dream landscapes.

name: René Magritte
bio: Belgian Surrealist painter who made familiar objects philosophically strange.
style: Deadpan realism, visual paradox, and displaced everyday objects.

name: Joan Miró
bio: Catalan painter whose work developed a playful language of abstract signs.
style: Biomorphic shapes, floating signs, and playful fields of color.

name: Frida Kahlo
bio: Mexican painter who explored identity, the body, and personal experience.
style: Frontal self-portraiture, symbolic objects, and vivid Mexican visual traditions.

name: Diego Rivera
bio: Mexican painter whose murals connect social history and public space.
style: Monumental figures, social narrative, and rhythmic fresco composition.

name: José Clemente Orozco
bio: Mexican muralist whose work presents a tragic vision of history.
style: Dramatic diagonals, expressive bodies, and critical historical allegory.

name: David Alfaro Siqueiros
bio: Mexican muralist who experimented with industrial materials and dynamic perspective.
style: Forceful foreshortening, sweeping motion, and politically charged imagery.

name: Tarsila do Amaral
bio: Brazilian modernist painter who helped shape the Anthropophagy movement.
style: Simplified monumental forms, tropical color, and Brazilian cultural references.

name: Candido Portinari
bio: Brazilian painter whose public art depicts labor and social experience.
style: Expressive figuration, monumental groups, and social narrative.

name: Wifredo Lam
bio: Cuban painter who joined modernist forms with Afro-Caribbean cultural imagery.
style: Hybrid figures, dense vegetation, and rhythms shaped by Cubism and Surrealism.

name: Jacob Lawrence
bio: American painter whose narrative series explore Black history and everyday life.
style: Angular figures, flat vivid colors, and sequential storytelling.

name: Aaron Douglas
bio: American painter associated with the Harlem Renaissance.
style: Silhouettes, concentric light, and rhythmic scenes of Black history.

name: Romare Bearden
bio: American artist whose paintings and collages explore African American experience.
style: Layered collage, shifting scale, and musical everyday narratives.

name: Alma Thomas
bio: American painter whose abstractions draw on nature and color.
style: Mosaic-like color marks, radiant patterns, and rhythmic abstraction.

name: Jean-Michel Basquiat
bio: American painter whose work combines street imagery, language, and historical critique.
style: Urgent marks, anatomical figures, crowns, and fragmented written language.

name: Jackson Pollock
bio: American Abstract Expressionist painter known for poured and dripped paint.
style: All-over rhythm, layered drips, and gestural movement across the canvas.

name: Mark Rothko
bio: Latvian-born American painter known for expansive fields of color.
style: Soft-edged rectangles, saturated color, and contemplative visual depth.

name: Georgia O'Keeffe
bio: American modernist painter known for flowers, bones, and Southwestern landscapes.
style: Enlarged natural forms, clear contours, and expansive color shapes.

name: Edward Hopper
bio: American painter whose urban and rural scenes explore modern solitude.
style: Sharp architectural light, still figures, and narrative ambiguity.

name: Katsushika Hokusai
bio: Japanese Edo-period painter and printmaker of landscapes and everyday subjects.
style: Bold contour, rhythmic waves, and dramatic contrasts of scale.

name: Utagawa Hiroshige
bio: Japanese ukiyo-e artist celebrated for landscape series.
work: Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi bridge and Atake
style: Unusual viewpoints, atmospheric weather, and lyrical landscape color.

name: Sesshū Tōyō
bio: Japanese Zen monk and master of monochrome ink landscape.
style: Expressive ink, changing spatial rhythms, and spare mountain landscapes.

name: Kitagawa Utamaro
bio: Japanese ukiyo-e artist known for portraits of women.
work: Three Beauties of the Present Day
style: Elegant contours, close-cropped figures, and nuanced expressions.

name: Ogata Kōrin
bio: Japanese Rinpa painter and designer known for decorative natural motifs.
style: Bold patterned surfaces, flowing water, and stylized seasonal forms.

name: Qi Baishi
bio: Chinese painter whose ink works find vitality in small natural subjects.
style: Economical brushwork, lively ink washes, and closely observed creatures.

name: Zhang Daqian
bio: Chinese painter who combined classical mastery with experimental splashed ink.
style: Sweeping ink, rich mineral color, and atmospheric mountain forms.

name: Xu Beihong
bio: Chinese painter and educator who joined ink traditions with Western realism.
work: Tian Heng and His Five Hundred Followers
style: Anatomical observation, vigorous horses, and expressive ink drawing.

name: Fan Kuan
bio: Northern Song Chinese landscape painter known for monumental mountain scenes.
style: Towering mountains, textured rock, and tiny human figures.

name: Guo Xi
bio: Northern Song Chinese landscape painter and theorist.
style: Layered mountain spaces, misty distance, and sinuous tree forms.

name: An Gyeon
bio: Joseon Korean court painter associated with classical landscape traditions.
work: Dream Journey to the Peach Blossom Land
style: Dreamlike mountain space, shifting viewpoints, and expressive ink texture.

name: Jeong Seon
bio: Joseon Korean painter renowned for true-view landscapes of Korean scenery.
style: Bold ink masses, specific mountain forms, and dramatic weather.

name: Kim Hong-do
bio: Joseon Korean painter celebrated for lively scenes of everyday life.
style: Economical lines, animated gesture, and observant scenes of ordinary labor.

name: Shin Yun-bok
bio: Joseon Korean painter known for genre scenes of social life.
style: Fine contours, delicate color, and attentive social observation.

name: Park Soo-keun
bio: Korean painter whose work depicts ordinary people and postwar daily life.
style: Granular surfaces, simplified figures, and muted earth colors.

name: Kim Whanki
bio: Korean painter who moved from lyrical figuration to all-over abstraction.
style: Rhythmic dots, deep blue fields, and spacious lyrical abstraction.

name: Raja Ravi Varma
bio: Indian painter who combined academic oil painting with Indian subjects.
style: Naturalistic figures, rich fabrics, and theatrical mythological storytelling.

name: Amrita Sher-Gil
bio: Hungarian-born Indian painter who helped shape modern Indian art.
style: Solid simplified figures, earthy color, and quiet psychological gravity.

name: Ben Enwonwu
bio: Nigerian painter and sculptor who combined modernist forms with local traditions.
style: Elegant figuration, rhythmic line, and luminous portrait color.

name: Gerard Sekoto
bio: South African painter and musician whose work depicts Black urban life.
style: Warm color, rhythmic figures, and humane scenes of everyday labor.
